reason: A shard measured it at 7.7 s against a budget of 15 s (#2965), on chromium rather than WebKit, pointing at a cost shared across projects rather than one browser's automation latency. Chapter I, II and III's beforeEach set reduced motion and afterEach put it back on every test, paying a media round trip twice a test for a preference that never changes within the file; it now moves to a file-level beforeAll/afterAll, cutting that cost from twice a test to twice a file. A clean ouro-chromium run of the whole file shows no change (6.4 s and 7 s for 16 tests, both under budget and within the run-to-run spread this session has measured for other media-round-trip fixes), so the remaining cost still reads as CI-shard load, not an avoidable wait this fix left behind. This entry's own project name was missing Vitest's own suffix (the project is named "site", and Vitest names a browser project's tests "site (chromium)"), so the exemption never matched and the test kept reporting as a fresh breach on #3032's main runs (45075449817, 8.3 s) despite this reasoning already standing; the fix here is the matching key, not a new cost. Revisit if a shard measures it slow again with headroom to spare.
